skill.name: one-answer
skill.description: Guides assistants to review context, verify available evidence, and plan complete steps before giving recommendations, safety answers, or status updates.
skill.summary: Prepare one recommendation with verified facts, ordered steps, and clearly labeled unknowns.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

security_audit.summary: All three reconnaissance matches are false positives in ordinary context review, uncertainty labeling, and planning guidance. No evidence found of malicious reconnaissance, exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md. The skill provides prose instructions rather than executable verification tools.

static_findings.snippet: 2. **Find what was already said or decided** on this topic: the conversation, project notes, client
- What you did not verify is labeled "not verified". Never present it as certain.
- Did I check the obvious trap and the safest order?

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 15 requests one or two topic-specific searches of conversation history, project notes, client files, or memory. This supports decision continuity, without directing system enumeration, secret collection, or data transmission.
Line 39 requires unverified claims to be labeled "not verified" and prohibits presenting them as certain. This is an accuracy rule, not an instruction to inspect systems or collect information.
Line 44 asks whether the plan accounts for obvious pitfalls and the safest order. The surrounding checklist concerns planning quality, with no reconnaissance commands or collection targets.

content.value_statement: Changing recommendations and incomplete plans create extra work for users. This skill guides assistants to check evidence, resolve planning gaps, and present one complete answer.
actual_capabilities: Directs assistants to review earlier decisions and relevant context before making recommendations.
Prompts available code, page, API, or screenshot checks before answering.
Structures plans around failure scenarios, reversible actions, and later irreversible steps.
Requires recommendations first, followed by complete ordered steps and relevant unknowns.
Requires source-based names, numbers, and identifiers instead of recalled values.
Consolidates essential clarification into one question with options.
limitations: Provides instructions only, without bundled scripts, integrations, or independent verification tools.
Verification depends on the assistant having suitable tools, permissions, and accessible evidence.
Cannot guarantee a correct first answer or eliminate later changes when new facts appear.
Does not define platform-specific integration rules or replace authoritative documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan an integration change
use_cases.description: Review account constraints, prior decisions, and failure scenarios before recommending the order of an integration migration.

use_cases.title: Report deployment status
use_cases.description: Separate observed deployment results from unverified assumptions before telling a team that a service is live.

use_cases.title: Choose an operational approach
use_cases.description: Compare options against existing team decisions, identify missing facts, and deliver one recommendation with complete steps.

prompt_templates.title: Give one clear recommendation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use one-answer to recommend [option A or option B] for [goal]. Review the context, lead with your recommendation, and label unverified facts.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a status claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Use one-answer to assess whether [service] is live. Check available evidence and separate confirmed observations from anything not verified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare an evidence-based status update.

prompt_templates.title: Build a complete change plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use one-answer to plan [change]. Respect prior decisions, check available documentation, consider failures, and put reversible steps before irreversible actions.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a constrained decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Use one-answer to evaluate [decision] under [constraints]. Review prior agreements, verify key assumptions, and identify dependencies. Ask one essential question if blocked.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reconcile conflicting constraints and missing evidence.

output_examples.input: The health endpoint returned success, but nobody tested sign-in. Can we tell the client the service is fully working?
output: Do not report the service as fully working yet.
Verified: the health endpoint returned success.
Not verified: sign-in and the main user workflow.
Test sign-in and the main workflow, then report those observed results.

output_examples.input: We agreed to use a test account first. Should I delete the old integration before testing the replacement?
output: Keep the old integration until the replacement passes testing.
Retain the agreed test-account approach and verify whether both integrations can coexist.
Test the replacement and prepare a rollback before switching production.
Delete the old integration only if needed after successful validation.
Not verified: whether the platform permits both integrations at once.

best_practices: Provide relevant prior decisions, constraints, and source documents before requesting a recommendation.
Allow appropriate verification checks and require clear labels for facts that remain unverified.
Review irreversible steps and obtain required approvals before taking action.
anti_patterns: Treating a single polished answer as proof that its claims are correct.
Requesting a verified status while withholding the evidence or access needed to check it.
Suppressing material corrections merely to avoid changing an earlier answer.

faq.question: What does one-answer do?
faq.answer: It guides assistants to review context, check available facts, plan complete steps, and present a recommendation before supporting details.

faq.question: Does it guarantee a correct first answer?
faq.answer: No. It provides a checklist, not a correctness guarantee. Missing evidence and new facts can still require revisions.

faq.question: Does it include verification tools?
faq.answer: No. It asks the assistant to use available checks but does not bundle scripts or integrations.

faq.question: How does it handle missing information?
faq.answer: It labels unverified facts and asks one question with options when user input is essential to the decision.

faq.question: Can it change earlier team decisions?
faq.answer: It requires user approval to change a user decision or team rule and places relevant new facts first.

faq.question: Should it hide important corrections?
faq.answer: No. Its guidance allows a concise correction when the change affects what the user will do.
